title: Kokuyaku Honzo Komoku (Japanese Ben Cao)
shelf_note: 1929 Japanese translation of the Bencao gangmu; the page is from the 主治 (indications) section, as the running head says.
rights_flag: A 1929 Japanese typeset translation (Shirai Mitsutaro); possibly still in copyright in Japan depending on the translators' death dates. Nothing on this leaf shows a licence.
structure_note: printed_backsteps 262 / repeats 105 on 535 numbered pages is high, but this book carries kanji page numbers that the OCR misreads (this leaf: printed 二一六, stored 三二六), so most backsteps are probably misread numerals, not a disordered scan.

title: Year book reports, 1332-1337
shelf_note: A manuscript of Law French year-book reports (Hilary term heading; Westoft/Elmedon avowry case; Shardelowe, Scrope as speakers).
structure_note: 275 of 335 pages OCR'd and 260 translated; 105 printed numbers with 28 backsteps is unremarkable for a manuscript with sporadic foliation.

ocr_errors.problem: two lines replaced by a repeating filler of stock law-French phrases ('par de la partie par de la seisine') with no mark of doubt; the feoffment to William, Robert's father, is lost

ocr_errors.problem: abbreviation expanded to 'aqua' (water); the English opens 'And water of this'

tr_errors.english: by the party by the seisin of which the seisin not said in ancient times …
tr_errors.problem: word-for-word rendering of the filler; most of the page reads as unintelligible English with no signal that the source is uncertain

pages.not_this_leaf_evidence: Lines 5–6 of the stored text ('par de la partie par de la seisine duns que la seisine nient / dist en auncien temps que ad de la partie par de la seisine') repeat stock phrases; the image there reads 'dist en avowant le quel ... enfeffa un Will' pere Robert' and similar, so this part of the text is fill, not the leaf's words. Hand is hard; confidence medium.

book_verdict: Right leaf and the case (Westoft/Elmedon avowry; Shardelowe, Scrope) is recognisable. But a dense legal hand has been read partly as fluent filler, and the English is a literal rendering of that filler, so most of the page cannot be trusted or followed.

title: བཀའ་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། མདོ་སྡེ། ས (Derge Kangyur, vol. 72)
shelf_note: Derge xylograph folio; text is the Kangyur passage comparing human and divine lifespans and their karmic causes.
structure_note: 619 of 620 folios have text (Esukhia e-text aligned per folio), only 4 translated; that matches a text-first import, not a defect.

other.note: <summary>/<keywords> blocks and Sanskrit glosses appended to the English; the glosses are reasonable (Trayastrimsha, Kalasutra) but are editorial additions.

book_verdict: The line openings and the passages I could read at this resolution (འགྱུར་རོ། །དགེ་སློང་དག་འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང་…; ཚེའི་ཚད་དོ། …; སུ་སྐྱེ་བར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། …) match the folio, and the English is faithful. I could not check every syllable of the small red xylograph.

title: Janma Kundali Dwadash Bhava Phalam
shelf_note: Short Devanagari jyotiṣa manuscript on the effects of planets in the twelve houses.

title: Полное собрание сочинений. Т. 9: Подросток
shelf_note: The leaf is Poor Folk (running head БѢДНЫЕ ЛЮДИ, p. 105), not The Adolescent; the volume title may be wrong (Poor Folk normally opens vol. 1 of the Marks edition), or this volume holds both. Worth a catalogue check.
structure_note: Printed 105 at scan 153 fits a volume with front matter. The catalogue title (Т. 9: Подросток) does not match the work on this page.

tr_errors.english: (absent: the English begins with the header and 'September 23.')
tr_errors.problem: the end of Makar's letter (five lines and his signature, including the 40 kopecks per sheet agreement) is dropped from the English of this page

other.note: Catalogue title says vol. 9 'The Adolescent'; the page is Poor Folk.

book_verdict: The transcription is near-perfect and the English of Varvara's letter is good, but the English drops the first five lines and signature of Makar's letter, and the volume is catalogued as The Adolescent while the page is Poor Folk.

title: Theonis Expositio in astronomiam
shelf_note: Greek astronomical manuscript (epicycles, apogee, precession of the equinoxes); consistent with Theon material.

ocr_errors.problem: abbreviations expanded to the wrong words in the first line

ocr_errors.image: ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀλεξάνδρου τελευτῆς(?)
ocr_errors.problem: an era (from the death of Alexander) read as the city Alexandria; the date sense of the passage is lost

tr_errors.source: χ̅ … τὸ κ’ αὐτῆς … τὰ δὲ κ’ τοῦ κέντρου
tr_errors.english: 'that of the 20' … 'before the 20' … 'And the 20 of the center'
tr_errors.problem: κ’ (the scribe's abbreviation for κέντρον, centre) and χ̅ (600) are both rendered as the number 20 throughout, so the figures in a numerical astronomical argument are wrong and the sentences meaningless

book_verdict: The transcription follows the leaf line by line, but this heavily abbreviated astronomical hand is often expanded wrongly. The English turns abbreviations and numerals into a wrong '20' throughout and reads as nonsense. I read the hand only partly at this resolution.

title: Jesuitici templi stupenda
shelf_note: Catalogued as Beringer's Latin anti-Jesuit pamphlet (Amberg 1610), but this leaf is the Hebrew title page of ספר עץ חיים (Etz Chaim, Lurianic Kabbalah) with its printing ban (מודעא רבא). The record's language field already says Hebrew. The title, author and date are of another work.
structure_note: 311 page records against pages_count 208, and this image is a split-crop (sp…) that cuts through the text block: the left ends of the Hebrew lines are cut off at the frame edge. A spread split along the wrong line or a spliced scan; the catalogue identity is wrong.

book_verdict: The page is the notice of approbations and the ten-year printing ban for Etz Chaim, read reasonably except where the crop cuts the line ends. It sits under the title of a 1610 Latin anti-Jesuit pamphlet. The catalogue identity is wrong, and the split cuts through the text.
